nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $(y_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $\mathbb{K}$ with $|y_i| \le 1$ for every $i$. The pairing with $y$ is the continuous linear functional $\ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K}) \to \mathbb{K}$ given by $x \mapsto \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} y_i x_i$.
nodes.title: Pairing $\ell^1$ with a sequence bounded by one
The $\ell^1$ norm is the sum of the coordinate norms

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $(y_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $\mathbb{K}$ with $|y_i| \le 1$ for every $i$. The continuous linear functional $x \mapsto \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} y_i x_i$ on $\ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ has operator norm at most $1$.
nodes.title: Pairing with a sequence bounded by one has norm at most one

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(x_n)$ be a sequence in $\ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, let $n' : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and let $M : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be such that every $i \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfies $i < M(j + 1)$ for some $j$. Every term $\sigma_i$ of the conjugate-sign sequence of $(x_n)$, $n'$ and $M$ satisfies $|\sigma_i| \le 1$.
nodes.title: The conjugate-sign sequence is bounded by one

nodes.summary: Let $M : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be monotone, and suppose every $i \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfies $i < M(j + 1)$ for some $j$. For all $k, i \in \mathbb{N}$ with $M(k) \le i < M(k + 1)$, the block index of $i$ (the least $j$ with $i < M(j + 1)$) is $k$.
nodes.title: Indices in block $k$ have block index $k$

nodes.summary: Let $M : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $M(0) = 0$, and suppose every $i \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfies $i < M(j + 1)$ for some $j$. For every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, if $k$ is the block index of $i$ (the least $k$ with $i < M(k + 1)$), then $M(k) \le i < M(k + 1)$.
nodes.title: An index lies in the block it is assigned to

nodes.summary: Let $M : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be such that every $i \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfies $i < M(k + 1)$ for some $k$. The block index of $i \in \mathbb{N}$ is the least $k$ with $i < M(k + 1)$.
nodes.title: Block index for a cutoff sequence

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(x_n)$ be a sequence in $\ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, let $n' : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and let $M : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be monotone and such that every $i \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfies $i < M(j + 1)$ for some $j$. Let $\sigma$ be the conjugate-sign sequence of $(x_n)$, $n'$ and $M$. For all $k, i \in \mathbb{N}$ with $M(k) \le i < M(k + 1)$, we have…
nodes.title: On block $k$, the conjugate signs recover absolute values

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(x_n)$ be a sequence in $\ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, let $n' : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and let $M : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be such that every $i \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfies $i < M(j + 1)$ for some $j$. For $i \in \mathbb{N}$, let $k$ be the block index of $i$ (the least $k$ with $i < M(k + 1)$) and let $v = x_{n'(k)}(i)$. The $i$-th term $\sigma_i$…
nodes.title: Conjugate-sign sequence of a block decomposition

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(x_n)$ be a sequence in $\ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, and let $x \in \ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. If $F(x_n) \to F(x)$ as $n \to \infty$ for every continuous linear functional $F : \ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K}) \to \mathbb{K}$, then $\|x_n - x\| \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Schur's theorem, norm form

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(x_n)$ be a sequence in $\ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and let $x_0 \in \ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. If $F(x_n) \to F(x_0)$ for every continuous linear functional $F$ on $\ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, that is, if $(x_n)$ converges weakly to $x_0$, then $x_n \to x_0$ in the $\ell^1$ norm.
nodes.title: Schur's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. If $y : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ satisfies $\|y_i\| \le 1$ for every $i$ and $x \in \ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, then the series $\sum_i y_i x_i$ is summable.
nodes.title: The pairing of $\ell^1$ with sequences bounded by $1$ is summable

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $b \in \mathbb{N}$, the series $\sum_{j=0}^{\infty} \|x_{j+b}\|$ is summable.
nodes.title: Tails of an $\ell^1$ sequence are absolutely summable

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $b \in \mathbb{N}$, $\sum_{j=0}^{\infty} \|x_{j+b}\| = \|x\| - \sum_{i < b} \|x_i\|$, where $\|x\|$ is the $\ell^1$ norm of $x$.
nodes.title: Tail of the norm series of an $\ell^1$ sequence

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be summable and let $a \le b$ be natural numbers. Then $\sum_{i=0}^{\infty} h(i)$ equals $\sum_{i < a} h(i) + \sum_{a \le i < b} h(i) + \sum_{j=0}^{\infty} h(j + b)$.
nodes.title: Splitting a series into a head, a middle block and a tail
